characterization_methods.key_findings: Rheological stress decreases with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (negative temperature-sensitive, positive strain-rate-sensitive); a peak stress is observed before softening.
characterization_methods.purpose: Perform the isothermal hot-compression test for this sample and obtain the rheological stress curve used for DRX analysis.
characterization_methods.technique: thermo-mechanical simulation (isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression) with rheological stress recording

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etchant 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction); images carry a 100 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 1050 °C/1 s^-1, zone 3 shows a fine, fairly equiaxed recrystallized grain structure with DRX basically completed, while zone 1 retains coarse grains with few long straight boundaries.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, then prepared, ground, polished and etched; three deformation zones imaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the microstructure/morphology of the three deformation zones to analyze DRX evolution.
characterization_methods.technique: optical / laser confocal microscopy of etched sections

analytical_models.equation_role: relates peak stress, temperature and strain rate; basis for the DRX activation energy

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Experimental range T = 900–1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.01–10 s^-1, which includes this sample's condition (1050 °C, 1 s^-1)
computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius hyperbolic sine constitutive analysis via linear regression of ln ε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)] and ln[sinh(ασp)] vs 1000/T
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Average fitted slopes k1 = 5.135 (Fig. 4a) and k2 = 15.690 (Fig. 4b); α = 0.00599; fitted lines not parallel, so activation energy is an average value.

analytical_models.equation_role: temperature-compensated strain rate characterizing combined effect of T and ε̇
analytical_models.model_note: Z = ε̇ exp(Qp/RT); lnZ for this exact sample condition (1050 °C, 1 s^-1) is 60.90.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: T = 900–1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.01–10 s^-1; lnZ tabulated for all 24 condition combinations
computational_details.simulation_method: Zener-Hollomon parameter calculation Z = ε̇ exp(Qp/RT) and tabulation of lnZ
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: lnZ increases with increasing ε̇ or decreasing T, matching the flow-stress trend.

analytical_models.equation_role: describes the flow curve and yields the material constant C, used to locate the DRX critical strain

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: σ/σp = [(ε/εp)exp(1−ε/εp)]^C; C obtained from linear fit of ln(σ/σp) vs [ln(ε/εp)+1−ε/εp]
computational_details.simulation_method: Cingara-McQueen equation combined with the Poliak-Jonas θ–σ inflection-point criterion to determine critical strain/stress of DRX
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Example fit at 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1: C = 0.1461, R = 0.9728; resulting εc/εp ≈ 0.452, consistent with literature for low-density high-strength steel.

analytical_models.equation_role: predict εc, σc, εp, σp, εs, σs as functions of lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Models derived by multiple linear regression; used to draw the DRX state diagram (Fig. 7).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Regression over the full experimental condition set (lnZ ≈ 52–71), which includes this sample's lnZ = 60.90
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: polynomial/linear regression models of characteristic values vs lnZ
computational_details.simulation_method: multiple linear regression of the flow-stress characteristic values (εc/σc, εp/σp, εs/σs) against the Zener-Hollomon parameter lnZ

analytical_models.equation_role: predicts DRX average grain size from temperature and strain rate
analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (eq. 11/12)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: drex = a·d0^h·ε^p·ε̇^q·exp(Q/RT) + b; with d0 and strain taken as fixed constants (a·d0^h·ε^p treated as a constant); condition range includes this sample (1050 °C, 1 s^-1)
computational_details.simulation_method: Levenberg-Marquardt optimization regression to build a DRX average grain size prediction model
computational_details.software_used: Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm; DEFORM-3D finite element software
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%; absolute error of predicted vs experimental grain size mostly within 3 µm.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as rigid plastic; die indenter set as rigid; semi-symmetric specimen to shorten simulation time; contact friction set to shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient between billet and air set to 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation matched the thermal compression experimental conditions.
computational_details.simulation_method: Finite element simulation of the hot-compression test
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Grain-size model validated against experiment with R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: grain size / degree of dynamic recrystallization (fine and uniform grain structure)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sample heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s as the first stage of the hot-compression schedule.
Sample homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 120 s.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 1050 °C at 5 °C/s.
Sample held 15 s at the set temperature before compression so that inside/outside temperature difference was eliminated.

Strain rate ε̇ = 1 s^-1 for this sample. Performed on a Gleeble-3500 simulator; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant were affixed to both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool it down.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression to 60% (maximum true strain 0.92) on a Gleeble-3500 thermomechanical simulator; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant on both end faces; compressed sample split in half along the axial axis for metallography.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Large grains relative to the 100 µm scale bar — individual grains span roughly one to a few times the bar length; a few grains appear almost featureless while others are densely striped.

structures.overall_structure: As-forged initial microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel: large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous, slightly etched boundaries enclosing dark grey grain interiors; nearly every grain interior contains many fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations (segregation banding) whose direction changes from grain to grain, indicating chemical heterogeneity in the as-forged condition.

structures.microstructure_counts: 3 deformation zones examined (1 difficult deformation, 2 small deformation, 3 large deformation)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Coarse grains with few, long straight boundaries; least dynamically recrystallized zone.

microstructure_list.region: zone 1 – difficult deformation zone (top/bottom centre near the loading surfaces)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Intermediate DRX degree between zone 1 and zone 3 (DRX degree order zone 3 > zone 2 > zone 1).

microstructure_list.region: zone 2 – small deformation zone (left/right ends near the horizontal centre line)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Fine, fairly equiaxed recrystallized grain structure; DRX basically completed in this zone at 1050 °C.

microstructure_list.region: zone 3 – large deformation zone (central band/core of the compression specimen)

structures.overall_structure: After 60% hot compression at 1050 °C/1 s^-1: the degree of dynamic recrystallization differs among the three deformation zones in the order zone 3 (large deformation) > zone 2 (small deformation) > zone 1 (difficult deformation). At 1050 °C the dynamic recrystallization is basically completed within the large-deformation zone, and recrystallized grain size grows with increasing temperature.

unmapped_findings: For this exact sample condition (T = 1050 °C, ε̇ = 1 s^-1) the Zener-Hollomon parameter is lnZ = 60.90 (Table 1, b0041) — a value specific to this sample.

The Fe-Mn-Al-C steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: its rheological stress increases with increasing ε̇ or decreasing T, and peak stress can be reduced by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (b0024, b0084).

The dynamic recrystallization activation energy calculated from the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine analysis is 669.844 kJ mol^-1, described as an average value over the experimental range because the fitted lines were not parallel (b0032, b0034, b0085).
For the Cingara-McQueen treatment the ratio εc/εp ≈ 0.452 was obtained, close to literature values for low-density high-strength steel, confirming the method (b0054).
The hot-deformation experiments on this steel batch/composition were stated to be reproducible under identical experimental conditions (b0018, b0024, b0058, b0065).
